key_insight: BiVerify improves mathematical self-correction by requiring the same candidate solution to pass both backward constraint checks and forward reasoning checks.
engineering_relevance: Pairing complementary verification directions can make LLM-based mathematical workflows more reliable than relying on either direction alone.
method: Start with backward verification against the original problem constraints, then check reasoning and objective completeness forward.
Dynamically switch directions, reset verification state, and revise candidates or verification flow based on outcomes.
Use shared mathematical tools to separate logical reasoning from precise computation.
evidence_signal: Across five challenging math benchmarks and multiple DeepSeek, GPT, and Gemini models, BiVerify reports a 13.5-percentage-point average accuracy gain over the strongest representative public baseline evaluated, reaching 31.2 points on GPT.
watch_item: Repeated verification and revision may add latency and computation cost; the abstract does not quantify this overhead.
paper_title: BiVerify: Closing the Loop Between Backward and Forward Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction
